extracted.intended_audience: public relations and crisis communication practitioners (press-release writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting press releases during organizational crises, matching response strategies to crisis type and reputational threat, and including standard release components and tactical recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benoit — Denial
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple denial or shifting blame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of Image Restoration Theory: use when organization seeks to assert it did not cause the wrongdoing or to attribute responsibility elsewhere. Includes outright denial and identifying scapegoats. Consider reputational risk if evidence contradicts denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benoit — Evasion of responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims of provocation, defeasibility, accident, or good intentions to avoid full responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to reduce perceived culpability by explaining circumstances (e.g., lack of intent, inability to foresee). May include arguing the event was accidental or caused by external provocations; risky if seen as shirking accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benoit — Reduction of offensiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies such as bolstering, minimization, differentiation, transcendence, attacking the accuser, or offering compensation to reduce perceived offensiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to lessen the negative evaluation of the act by emphasizing positive aspects, contextualizing harm as minor, or reframing the act. Examples: reminding audiences of past good deeds (bolstering), comparing the harm to worse acts (differentiation), or providing compensation as a pragmatic remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benoit — Corrective action
rubrics_metrics.description: Promise to fix the problem and prevent recurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete commitments to change procedures, repair damage, or implement safeguards. Credibility depends on specificity and demonstrable follow-through; often paired with timelines and named responsible parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benoit — Mortification
rubrics_metrics.description: Apology and seeking forgiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full admission of responsibility plus apology. Best when organization accepts blame and offers remediation. Tone, sincerity, and follow-up actions determine effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCCT — Match response to crisis responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Crisis managers should match strategic crisis responses to the level of crisis responsibility and reputational threat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the crisis type (victim, accidental, preventable) and choose responses that align with attributed responsibility to stakeholders. Matching reduces reputational damage; mismatches (e.g., denying a preventable crisis) can worsen trust loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCCT — Deny response group
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses that deny or shift blame: victim, scapegoat, attack the accuser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate primarily for crises where the organization is clearly a victim or has low/no responsibility. Use cautiously; if evidence later contradicts denial, reputational damage will increase.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCCT — Diminish response group
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses that excuse or justify the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempt to reduce perceived intent or harm by explaining causes. Best for medium-responsibility (accidental) crises. Overuse can be perceived as evasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCCT — Rebuild response group
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses involving compensation and apology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended for high-responsibility (preventable) crises where the organization must accept blame and repair relationships through apology and reparations.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCCT — Bolstering (supplementary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary messages reminding stakeholders of past good works or using ingratiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used alongside primary strategies to remind audiences of the organization's positive attributes; should not replace responsibility-taking when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis type — Victim cluster (low responsibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crisis types where the organization is a victim: natural disaster, rumor, workplace violence, product tampering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders attribute low responsibility; deny-type responses or instructive/supportive communications are generally appropriate. Emphasize safety and support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis type — Accidental cluster (medium responsibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crises due to challenges or technical errors: technical-error accidents, technical-error product harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderate responsibility suggests diminish strategies (excuse/justification) and corrective actions; include factual explanations and steps to prevent recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis type — Preventable cluster (high responsibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crises caused by human error or organizational misdeeds: human-error accidents, human-error product harm, organizational misdeeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High responsibility requires rebuild strategies (apology, compensation) plus corrective action and transparent accountability measures to repair reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match response strategy to crisis type
rubrics_metrics.description: Match response strategy to crisis type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit operational rule: choose denial, diminish, rebuild, or bolstering based on whether the crisis is victim, accidental, or preventable. Ensures strategy credibility and reduces reputational threat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer rebuild for preventable crises
rubrics_metrics.description: For preventable crises: rebuild strategies (apology, compensation) work best.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the organization is clearly responsible, apology and compensation are most effective; combine with corrective actions and transparent accountability to restore trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge stakeholders' concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge stakeholders' concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly recognize affected parties' feelings and legitimate worries in the release. This builds empathy and reduces anger; a perfunctory mention is less effective than specific acknowledgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide instructional information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide instructional information (how to stay safe).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give clear, actionable steps for stakeholders to protect themselves during the crisis (e.g., evacuation instructions, product return procedures). Prioritize clarity and immediacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide adjusting information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide adjusting information (psychological support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer information that helps stakeholders cope emotionally (support resources, counseling lines, guidance on next steps). This complements factual/instructional content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Be timely - first hours are critical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue initial communication quickly to shape narratives and reassure stakeholders. Timeliness increases perceived competence even if full facts are not yet available; promise follow-ups when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be consistent across channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Be consistent across channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure messages on social media, press releases, briefings, and websites align to avoid confusion and mixed signals; designate approvals and monitoring to keep consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designate a single spokesperson
rubrics_metrics.description: Designate single spokesperson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a trained, authoritative spokesperson to reduce mixed messages and build credibility; provide media coaching and talking points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide regular updates even with no new information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide regular updates even when no new info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular check-ins reassure stakeholders and demonstrate ongoing engagement; if no new facts, reiterate what is known and the timeline for next update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use press briefings for viral crises
rubrics_metrics.description: Use press briefings when crisis goes viral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the crisis attracts wide attention, use briefings to manage flow of information, answer questions, and show leadership presence. Coordinate media logistics and key messages in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release component — Acknowledgment of incident
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgment of incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start the release by acknowledging that an incident occurred; clarity avoids speculation and shows transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release component — Expression of concern for affected
rubrics_metrics.description: Expression of concern for affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include empathy language for victims, employees, or customers; be specific about who is affected where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release component — Facts known so far
rubrics_metrics.description: Facts known so far.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise, verifiable information about what is currently known. Avoid speculation; label unconfirmed information as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release component — Actions being taken
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions being taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail immediate steps the organization is taking to address the situation and protect stakeholders, including investigations, safety measures, and corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release component — Support resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Support resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List help available to affected parties (hotlines, counseling, shelters, return/exchange procedures). Make access information clear and specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release component — Promise of updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Promise of updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit to providing further information and specify anticipated timing or conditions for the next update to manage expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release component — Contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact information for more info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear contact (name, role, phone, email, media office) so reporters and stakeholders can obtain further details; ensure spokesperson availability aligns with provided contact.
